To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

40% energy intake restriction (CEIR) of nulliparous C/O mice suppresses mammary tumor virus transcription and prevents development of spontaneous tumors, yet permits conception, gestation and lactations with comparable success to that of ad libitutum fed mice.

dietary energy intake restriction of C3 H/Ou mice suppresses mouse mamary tumor virus proviral expression in mammary epithelium even after mammary gland involution, and permits normal parturution and lactation but reduces litter size when dietary restriction is maintained during pregnancy and lactaion.
dietary restriction suppresses MMTV transcription in mice, and dietary restriction suppresses mammary tumor development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dietary energy intake in the etiology of mammary cancer and other chronic diseases.
the role of dietary restriction on mammary tumor development and on the expression of the mouse Mammary Tumor Virus.
the effects of dietary restriction on the development of mammary cancer in the C3H/Ov mouse, a strain that develops mammary adenocarinomas at high rates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary restriction is an effective means of suppressing mammary tumor development and MMTV proviral transcription, and of maintaining reproductive competence in C3H/Oul mice.

dietary restriction suppresses mammary tumor development by suppressing MMTV transcription in the mammary gland, and that dietary restriction does not suppress mammary MMTVs in the absence of mammary gland involution.
the suppression of MMTV proviral transcription in the mammary gland of CEIR mice is due to the dietary restriction per se, and not due to the interruption of the lactation period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dietary restriction of mice suppresses mammary tumor development by suppressing mammary MMTv transcription, and that the nutritional demands of pregnancy and lactation are essential for normal mammary development and lactation, but not for normal mammary MMTtv expression or tumor suppression.

1) dietary restriction of C57BL/6J and C3H/OU mice prevents development of mammary tumors by suppressing expression of mouse mammary tumor provirus, 2) the level of Mtv transcription is rigorously regulated by the level of dietary energy intake, and 3) dietary restriction does not impair reproductive performance in C3H/Ov mice.

dietary energy restriction of C3h/Ou mice suppresses mammary expression of MMTV and prevents mammary adenocarcioma in uniparous and multiparous mice, and that dietary energy restriction during pregnancy and lactations permits normal conception, parturition, lactation, weaning of lits and production of healthy lits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary restriction can be imposed on nulliparous mice, interrupted by mating and continued only in pregnancy and lactation.

dietary energy level can have profound effects on mammary tumor development and on the expression of the MMTV provirus, which can be separated from the effects of dietary energy on the hormonal milieu of the mouse mamary gland.
dietary restriction is a potent means of suppressing mammary tumor development and MMTV gene expression, and it can be accomplished without compromising reproductive function.
